commitResults.messageBody:
Add Java assertions to document the assumptions that should hold if the parser, task list, and storage logic are used correctly.

The parser now asserts the expected number of parsed parts for deadline and event commands, and the shared keyword parser asserts that at least one keyword is supplied. TaskList now asserts that get and delete are called only with valid one-based task numbers. Storage now asserts that the fallback task creation branch is only reached for event tasks.

These assertions do not replace user-facing error handling. Existing DukeyException checks remain responsible for invalid user input and malinformed save file data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make storage task type handling explicit
commitResults.messageBody:
Refactor Storage#createTask so each supported task type is handled by an explicit branch.

The code quality guide recommends using the final else branch only for the true default case, not as the last known option. The previous implementation relied on the final else branch to mean event task, which made the reader remember that earlier validation had already filtered out unknown task types.

This change stores the task type in a clearly named local variable, checks the event case explicitly, and keeps the final path for invalid task types. That makes the happy path clearer while preserving the existing user-facing error handling for malformed save data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use switch for parser command dispatch
commitResults.messageBody:
Refactor Parser#parse so command dispatch is expressed as a switch over CommandWord.

The code quality guide emphasizes readability and logical structure. The previous implementation used a long if-else chain, which made the supported command mapping harder to scan as the number of commands grew.

This change first handles the unknown-command case explicitly, then keeps the valid command paths in one switch. The behavior and user-facing error messages remain the same, but the parser now communicates that it is choosing among enum command values.

Replace storage parsing literals and array indexes with named constants.

The code quality guide recommends avoiding magic literals because they force readers to infer meaning from raw values. Storage parsing used values such as T, D, E, 0, 1, and several numeric indexes directly in the parsing logic.

This change gives those file-format fields descriptive names, such as TASK_TYPE_INDEX, DESCRIPTION_INDEX, DONE_STATUS, and EVENT_TASK_TYPE. The behavior remains unchanged, but the code now explains the storage format at the point where it is parsed.

Refactor Parser#parseByKeywords so keyword boundary detection is described by named helper methods.

The code quality guide recommends avoiding complicated expressions because dense boolean logic makes readers pause to decode intent. The old loop embedded the full boundary check directly in the while condition.

This change extracts that logic into findKeywordIndex, isKeywordDelimited, isStartOfWord, and isEndOfWord. The parsing behavior remains the same, but the main keyword-splitting loop now reads at a higher level of abstraction.

Replace raw indexes into parser result arrays with named constants.

The code quality guide recommends avoiding magic values because they hide intent. Parser methods used positions such as parts[0], parts[1], and parts[2] to refer to descriptions and date fields after keyword parsing.

This change names those positions as DESCRIPTION_INDEX, DEADLINE_BY_INDEX, EVENT_FROM_INDEX, and EVENT_TO_INDEX. The parsing behavior remains unchanged, but command construction and validation now reveal what each parsed part represents.

Replace the null result from Parser#parseCommand with CommandWord.UNKNOWN.

The code quality guide recommends making code obvious and avoiding things that trip up the reader. Returning null from parseCommand forced callers and tests to understand a special sentinel outside the command enum.

This change keeps command recognition inside the CommandWord enum by adding UNKNOWN. Parser#parse now checks that explicit value, and the parser test documents the expected result for command-like prefixes that are not real commands.

Add optional completion timestamps to tasks and expose task-list statistics for completed and pending work.

The stats feature needs to distinguish tasks that are done from tasks that were completed during the current calendar week or month. The previous model stored only a boolean done status, so it could not support time-based insights accurately.

This commit keeps existing markAsDone behavior for older loading paths while adding an overload that records a LocalDateTime. TaskList now provides aggregate counting methods, and unit tests cover calendar week, calendar month, and unknown completion-date cases.

Introduce a dedicated stats command that reports total, completed, pending, current-week, and current-month task counts. The command validates that no extra arguments are supplied, matching the approved feature scope.

Record completion timestamps when tasks are marked so the runtime statistics can distinguish recent completions. Inject a Clock through Dukey and Parser to keep time-sensitive behavior deterministic in tests.

Add the matching GUI response style and JUnit coverage for command parsing, invalid stats input, and end-to-end stats output.

Extend the task storage format with an optional completion timestamp so stats can still report recent completions after the app restarts.

Keep older saved rows valid by treating missing completion timestamps as unknown. Validate malformed timestamps and reject undone saved tasks that incorrectly contain a completion timestamp.

Update task serialization and storage tests for todo, deadline, and event rows in both old and new formats.

Update the user guide with the stats command, its no-argument validation rule, and the way completion timestamps affect current-week and current-month counts.

Extend the UI test plan with valid and invalid stats command scenarios. Adjust expected saved data for commands that rewrite loaded tasks using the new storage format.

Add tests/test-plan.md as a high-level pointer to the detailed UI plan and the JUnit coverage used for the statistics feature.

Polish the JavaFX chat window so the conversation is easier to scan in a small app window. The update reduces avatar size, tightens message spacing, and gives reply bubbles clearer visual separation from user messages.

Allow the main window to resize from a practical minimum size while keeping the input bar and chat area anchored. This satisfies the A-BetterGui increment with changes focused on usability rather than decorative graphics.

Give Dukey a consistent calm task-librarian voice in greetings, confirmations, errors, and farewell messages. This adds a recognizable personality while preserving command syntax and task formatting.

Update the GUI greeting, user guide, JUnit expectations, and CLI UI test plan so the documented and tested behavior matches the new user-facing tone.

Handle common command-format mistakes more deliberately. Commands now tolerate leading and trailing spaces, while deadline and event parsing rejects duplicated delimited keywords instead of treating them as part of a date/time value.

Add parser and UI test coverage for the new validation paths so the behavior remains stable for both direct parser use and full CLI sessions.

Increase coverage around the main Dukey#getResponse workflows that users exercise most often. The new tests cover add/list/find, mark/unmark/delete, and date-based listing through the full parser-command-storage path.

Document the added workflow coverage in the test plan so the project testing strategy reflects the A-MoreTesting increment.

Tidy project-facing documentation for the final feature pass. The root README now describes Dukey as the actual app instead of a starter template, and the user guide credits the course template, JavaFX tutorial structure, and tutorial avatar resources.

Rename the shadow JAR output to dukey.jar so the generated release artifact matches the product name rather than the original Duke starter name.

Make deadline and event display formatting independent of platform-specific AM/PM casing. GitHub Actions on Ubuntu formats the marker as PM, while the local macOS run produced pm, causing exact-output tests to fail in CI.

Normalize only the AM/PM marker so month names keep their expected title case and existing user-facing output remains unchanged.

GitHub Actions runs tests on Windows as well as Unix-like systems. PrintStream.println uses the platform line separator, which made getResponse return CRLF on Windows while tests compare against LF-separated GUI response strings.

Normalize only the captured getResponse text to LF before trimming it. This keeps console output and storage writes platform-native while making the GUI-facing response API deterministic across CI environments.
